newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour group calls on party to oppose EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour group calls on party to oppose EMU.

text.p: A parliamentary group within the UK opposition Labour Party is to call on leader Tony Blair at next week's party conference to oppose a European single currency.
The group, headed by MP Austin Mitchell and including former ministers Peter Shore and Denzil Davies, is holding a public meeting on Sunday at the start of the conference in Blackpool.

In a news release ahead of the meeting, the Labour Euro-Safeguards Campaign group said the party will have to make a decision on a single currency soon after the next election which is due to be held sometime in the next eight months.

"Maastricht terms require heavy cuts in public expenditure and the transfer of economic power to unaccountable central bankers. Labour should make it clear in its general election manifesto that it will not travel the Maastricht road," the group said in its release.
A member of the group, Labour MP Nigel Spearing, said the number of its supporters was small.
But he said the group's aim was to ensure detailed debate about the single currency before a decision was taken.

Official Labour party policy is to maintain Britain's opt-out negotiated by Conservative Prime Minister John Major and only join a single currency if the economic conditions are right and it is in Britain's interests.
But there is opposition in Major's party to these policies.
Earlier this year around 50 Labour MP's signed a motion opposing British entry into a single currency.
